title: BackendV1Call
description: One call to an EKKA backend adapter (`ekka.backend` v1) as the adapter receives it on its Unix socket: the operation, the path values its route names, the three required headers and the strict body. The route for each operation is in operations.json. The answer is `$defs.result`. The adapter verifies the Govern-signed gate token in `x-ekka-gate-token` offline before it reads anything else, enforces the limits the token carries (governance/grant-constraints), and never answers with a backend's own error text. Nothing in this contract names a backend's API: the adapter's driver turns each operation into its backend's calls.

name.description: The `{name}` value of the route: the desk's name.

provider.description: The `{provider}` value of the route: a provider's name.

operation.description: The backend operations. provider_connect creates a provider or replaces its selected credentials through the governed local-only credential transport.

resource_version.description: The backend's version of a desk's configuration, as the adapter last read it. A change that names one is applied only if the desk is still at that version, so two admins never overwrite each other.

headers.description: Header names in lowercase, as HTTP compares them. The API gate adds all four on every call to the adapter, and a plan cannot set any of them.

x-ekka-gate-token.description: Base64 of the Govern-signed gate token (governance/gate-token.schema.json) for exactly this call: organization, API-gate instance, resource `apis/desks`, operation and expiry. Its `scope.contract` is `ekka.gate.api.v1`, the API gate's contract that Govern signs; the backend protocol is never in the token, it is `x-ekka-backend-contract`. The grant's limits are under `constraints.grant`, checked against governance/grant-constraints/desks.v1.schema.json; `constraints.body_sha256` beside it pins this call's body. Verified offline against Govern's published `gate_token` key. Never logged.

authorization.description: The backend's administration credential, placed by the organization in the Enclave's vault and injected by the API gate on each call. The adapter keeps no credential at rest. Never logged.

x-ekka-operation-id.description: `<run id>/<step id>/<task id>`: the fully qualified execution identity. Govern mints a fresh task id for every execution of an operation, so two operations that each hold a step with the same id, a new visit of a looping operation and a workflow retry all get distinct ids, while a redelivery of the same task keeps its id. The adapter records it with a digest of the request before it calls the backend: the same id with the same request answers the recorded outcome with `delivery: duplicate`, and the same id with a different request is refused OPERATION_ID_REUSED. Its run id must equal the token's.

x-ekka-backend-contract.description: The backend protocol this call speaks. Read from this header, never from the token. An adapter refuses a call naming a protocol it does not serve.

x-ekka-provider-credentials.description: Only for provider_connect: base64 of a JSON object mapping credential names to secret strings. Injected from the local Enclave vault after authorization, never set by a plan, recorded, logged or sent to Govern. Its keys must exactly equal body.credential_refs keys. An empty object is used for a keyless provider. Total decoded JSON is at most 8192 bytes; values are nonempty one-line strings. The adapter holds it in memory only and never copies it into operation records. Other operations refuse this header.

resources.description: A desk's CPU and memory limit, which the kernel enforces on the desk's sandbox. `cpu_millicores`: thousandths of one CPU, so 2000 is two CPUs; the backend applies it as the CPU quota (on Linux cgroup v2, `cpu.max` reads `<cpu_millicores x 100> 100000`). `memory_mib`: mebibytes; the backend applies it as the memory limit (`memory.max` reads `memory_mib x 1048576`). Whole numbers only, so a limit is read back exactly, never rounded: written as JSON integers, such as `2000`. A JSON Schema validator also accepts `2000.0` as an integer, but the adapter refuses it as REQUEST_INVALID, because reading it through a float could round a fraction into a whole number.

cpu_millicores.description: Thousandths of one CPU: 100 is a tenth of a CPU, 256000 is 256 CPUs.

memory_mib.description: Mebibytes: 256 is the least a desk is given, 4194304 is 4 TiB.

image.description: The image by digest, never a tag, in one of two forms. `<name>@sha256:<64 hex>`: an image from a registry, by its registry digest. `sha256:<64 hex>` alone: an image the machine built itself, by its local content ID (Docker's image ID, `docker image inspect --format '{{.Id}}'`), which the backend uses as it is and never pulls. The two are different hashes of one image, so a registry digest never matches a content ID. The digest (after `@`, or the whole value) must be in the limits' `image_digests`; hex is lowercase and exactly 64 characters.

policy.description: The desk's starting network policy, in the backend's own form, which the adapter's driver reads. Its digest, computed by the adapter, must be in the limits' `policy_digests`, and every host it allows must be inside `allowed_hosts`.

providers.description: Providers to attach, each in the limits' `providers`, with its configuration matching `provider_config_digests`.

environment.description: Plain environment values. Each name must be in the limits' `environment_keys`. Never a secret: a provider carries secrets.

resources.description: The desk's CPU and memory limit. Required: a desk is never created without one. Each value must be at most the limits' `resources` (`max_cpu_millicores`, `max_memory_mib`), and a grant without `resources` allows no create; either is refused CONSTRAINT_RESOURCES. The adapter sends it to the backend with the create and answers `ready` only when the backend's own record of the desk carries exactly this limit, else `unknown`.

repo.description: Not used, and kept only so an older caller's empty value is not refused. A repository reaches a desk through a setup plan run on the desk, never through create. A non-empty value is refused FIELD_NOT_ALLOWED; absent or empty is the same.

policy.description: The whole resulting policy, in the backend's own form. Every host it allows must be inside the limits' `allowed_hosts`.

approval_mode_body.description: Turn a discovery desk's proposal approval mode on or off. `auto`: the backend may approve the desk's own network proposals, and only while the adapter's permit for the desk's sandbox id is valid. The adapter allows it only for a desk inside the grant's open `discovery` window (its name starts with the window's `name_prefix`, its image digest is in the window's `image_digests`, every provider attached is in the window's `providers`), sets the backend's setting, reads it back as applied, and only then writes the permit. `manual`: the adapter deletes the permit first, then sets the backend's setting and reads it back; turning auto off is always allowed for a desk the adapter manages.

code.description: Why an answer is refused, or what is not known. A CONSTRAINT_ code names the limit that refused it. Our own words only: a backend's error text is never forwarded. DESK_BUSY: the desk is held by a running job or another change; nothing changed, and the change may be asked again once the desk is free. CONSTRAINT_CREDENTIAL_ENDPOINT: a policy change would add, change or move a network endpoint that carries a provider's credentials; it has no limit of its own, because changing where a provider's credentials reach is a provider change, made at install, never a policy change. NOT_APPLIED: the change never reached the desk; nothing changed. DESK_NOT_DISCOVERY: the desk is not one a discovery window allows (no `discovery` in the grant, a name without its `name_prefix`, an image digest or a provider outside its lists), or, on the evidence read, the desk has no permit; nothing changed. DISCOVERY_WINDOW_CLOSED: the grant's `discovery` window has expired; nothing changed. APPROVAL_MODE_NOT_APPLIED: the backend's setting, read back, is not the mode asked for; the adapter wrote no permit and set the desk back to manual. CONSTRAINT_RESOURCES: a create asks more CPU or memory than the limits' `resources` allow, or the limits carry no `resources`; nothing changed.

result.description: Every answer is in this closed shape. `ready`, `refused` and `unknown` are sent with HTTP 200; `running` is sent with HTTP 202, and only when a change reaches the adapter's deadline. Both are 2xx, so the API gate reads the facts either way; a step's facts come only from a 2xx answer, by field name. The fact a plan reads is `outcome` itself, declared with enum `ready|refused|unknown`, and `desk_ready`. The enum leaves out `running` on purpose: a 202 fails the plan's fact check on arrival and the step fails closed. `delivery` says whether this answer is new or recorded, so a refusal delivered twice stays refused. `desk_ready` is written from `outcome` by the table in operations.json, and this schema refuses an answer that disagrees with it.

delivery.description: `first`: this call did the work. `duplicate`: this operation id was already answered, and this is the recorded answer; nothing was sent to the backend again.

outcome.description: `ready`: done, and the desk is ready. `refused`: nothing changed; `code` says why. `unknown`: the change completed or stopped (a settle marker proved it), but the resulting desk does not match the request; a person checks before any retry. `running`: the change reached the adapter's deadline and is not finished; only ever an HTTP 202, carrying `operation_id`. The next `status` of that desk reconciles it.

backend_id.description: The backend's id for the desk. It stays on the customer's machine: a plan declares no fact for it.

policy.description: The desk's live policy: the revision it has LOADED, as `openshell.sandbox.v1.SandboxPolicy` in proto3 JSON, the canonical form `policy_digest` is computed from. Sent only by the policy read (`GET /v1/desks/{name}/policy`, operation `policy_get`), only with outcome `ready` and beside its `policy_digest`, and only when its JSON is at most 65536 bytes: a larger policy is left out and `policy_digest` still names it. A policy names paths, hosts and ports, never a secret.

providers_digest.description: On `status`: EKKA's digest of the desk's providers, computed by the adapter over the gateway's provider records, so the Enclave can re-pin after a governed disconnect.

resources.description: With outcome `ready` only, on an answer that reads one desk back (`create`, `stop`, `start`, `status`, `policy_get`, `policy_set`, `provider_detach`, `approval_mode`): the CPU and memory limit the backend holds for the desk, as the adapter read it. Left out for a desk the backend holds with no limit, or with one this contract cannot state. It is the backend's record of the desk, not a reading of the kernel: the Enclave compares the kernel's own values with it before any work starts on the desk.

approval_mode.description: On an `approval_mode` answer: the desk's proposal approval mode, as the adapter read it back from the backend after setting it. Sent only with outcome `ready`.

permit_expires_at.description: With `approval_mode: auto` only, and always with it: when the permit the adapter wrote for the desk's sandbox id expires, UTC. The earlier of the discovery window's end and 60 minutes after the permit was written.

evidence.description: On a `discovery_evidence` answer only, with outcome `ready`: what a discovery desk's network proposals and traffic showed (discovery-evidence.v1.schema.json). At most 262144 bytes (256 KiB) as JSON; a schema cannot measure that, so the adapter enforces it and a reader refuses a larger one.

operation_id.description: On `running` only: the operation still in progress, as the adapter's request id for it, a lowercase hyphenated UUID. It is the id the desk's lock names and the id `ekka desk release --operation` and `up.sh desks settle --operation` take; never the call's `X-EKKA-Operation-Id`, which is only the input.

provider_fact.description: One provider the gateway holds in the adapter's configured workspace (`backend_gateway.workspace`), as `grant_facts` answers it. `name` is the provider's own name (`Provider.metadata.name`), the name a desk and a grant use, never its profile's type. It carries EITHER its `digest` (what a desks grant's `provider_config_digests` holds for that name, computed by the adapter's own function over the gateway's provider record and the profile it names) OR a `code` saying why there is none. Never both, never neither. A provider listed here grants nothing: the reader keeps only the providers its own installation's profile set names.

code.description: `PROVIDER_PROFILE_MISSING`: the gateway holds the provider but not the profile it names. `PROVIDER_UNREADABLE`: the gateway did not answer for it.

grant_facts.description: On a `grant_facts` answer only, and on every `ready` one: what a desks grant's limits are built from, computed by the adapter with the functions it enforces them with. A reader refuses a `ready` grant_facts answer that carries no `grant_facts`. Digests and names only: never a credential, a profile's secret or a policy's content. On this route `desk_ready: true` is the table's word for `ready` and says nothing about any desk.

baseline_policy_digest.description: The digest of the installation's baseline policy, which the adapter reads from `/etc/ekka-backend/baseline-policy.json` (mounted read-only by the installer; no request names a path): an `openshell.sandbox.v1.SandboxPolicy` in proto3 JSON, digested in the canonical form `policy_digest` uses. No baseline, no answer: the read is refused `BASELINE_POLICY_MISSING`, `BASELINE_POLICY_UNREADABLE` or `BASELINE_POLICY_INVALID`.

providers.description: Every provider the gateway holds in the adapter's workspace, read whole (every page), each name once; empty only when it holds none. A list that cannot be read whole is never answered short or empty: the read is refused `PROVIDERS_UNREADABLE`. More than 64 is refused `PROVIDERS_TOO_MANY`, never cut. The schema cannot see a repeated name; a reader refuses an answer that repeats one.

provider_connect_body.description: Provider identifiers and local credential references only. Existing non-secret configuration stays on the backend and is preserved during rotation; a new provider starts with empty explicit config. No config or credential value is a plan input. The grant must allow name and its resulting provider_config_digest, computed with REDACTED credential values. Absent expected_resource_version means create only; present means update only, exactly at that version. On update the type and profile workspace must match the existing provider; credential updates merge into its existing credential names, and the resulting full configuration must match the grant. Credential values never occur in this body. Each credential_ref is a random UUID issued by privileged providers_stage IPC, naming a one-use entry in the Enclave-only DESK_PROVIDER_CREDENTIAL_ namespace. It is never a caller-supplied vault path or a credential digest. The entry expires after ten minutes, cannot be overwritten through generic secret writes, and is atomically removed before its single send. A failed or interrupted attempt requires staging again. The API gate reads these entries only for the authorized local apis/desks POST /v1/providers call after validating the signed body pin and connection binding. The backend never resolves vault references. A duplicate replays its saved result without another write; an unresolved credential write is not automatically reissued after a restart because its secret is not recorded.

provider_info.description: Local provider metadata for native connection setup. No configuration values, credential values or customer content. An absent resource_version means the provider does not exist yet; a present version is required on the ensuing rotation. The adapter resolves the effective profile with the same precedence used by writes.

configuration_digest.description: The existing provider configuration digest, or the proposed empty-config digest for a keyless or single-credential profile using its default credential name. A grant can therefore be prepared before the first credential is set. Values are REDACTED when computing it; this is never a credential-value digest. Absent when a multi-credential new provider needs an explicit configuration choice.
